title: Bipartite Subset Graphs with Intersection Threshold Two Are List Colorable for Every Parameter at Least Five
abstract: For an integer $k \ge 2$ and an integer threshold $r \ge 0$, the bipartite subset graph $G(k,r)$ has vertex classes $A$ and $B$, two disjoint copies of the family $\binom{[2k-1]}{k}$ of all $k$-element subsets of $\{1, \dots, 2k-1\}$, with an edge between $a_S \in A$ and $b_T \in B$ if and only if $|S \cap T| \le r$. Give every vertex its own subset as its list, and let $r^*(k)$ be the least $r$ for which these standard lists admit no proper coloring. arXiv:2610.42094 shows that $r^2 > 2(2k-1)\ln(2k-1)$ forces uncolorability, so $r^*(k) = O(\sqrt{k \ln k})$, and notes that its method says nothing about the true least $r$. We prove two facts on the other side. First, standard-list colorability at a fixed threshold $r$ passes from $k$ to $k+1$, so $r^*(k)$ is nondecreasing in $k$. Second, $G(5,2)$ is colorable from its standard lists, by a single rule on $\mathbb{Z}_9$ used on both sides. Together they give that $G(k,2)$ is colorable from its standard lists for every $k \ge 5$, that is, $r^*(k) \ge 3$ for all $k \ge 5$. All statements are checked in Lean 4.
introduction:
The list chromatic number, or choosability, of a graph is a central parameter in graph theory. In arXiv:2610.42094, an investigation of list colorability in bipartite graphs introduces a family of bipartite subset graphs whose list colorability properties under standard list assignments provide lower bounds on bipartite choosability.

For an integer $k \ge 2$ and an integer $r \ge 0$, the bipartite subset graph $G(k,r)$ is defined with two vertex classes $A$ and $B$, each isomorphic to the family $\binom{[2k-1]}{k}$ of all $k$-element subsets of a ground set of $2k-1$ elements, denoted $[2k-1] = \{1, \dots, 2k-1\}$. Two vertices $a_S \in A$ and $b_T \in B$ are joined by an edge if and only if their defining subsets satisfy the intersection condition $|S \cap T| \le r$. There are no edges within $A$ or within $B$, making $G(k,r)$ a bipartite graph. Each vertex is assigned its indexing subset as its list of available colors: $L(a_S) = S$ for all $a_S \in A$, and $L(b_T) = T$ for all $b_T \in B$. A proper list coloring from these standard lists is a choice of a color $c(a_S) \in S$ for each $a_S \in A$ and a color $c(b_T) \in T$ for each $b_T \in B$ such that whenever $|S \cap T| \le r$, the chosen colors differ: $c(a_S) \ne c(b_T)$.

The least uncolorable intersection parameter $r^*(k)$ is defined as the minimum integer $r \ge 0$ such that $G(k,r)$ has no proper list coloring from its standard list assignment $L$. In arXiv:2610.42094, Theorem 1.3 establishes that the condition $r^2 > 2(2k-1)\ln(2k-1)$ is sufficient to guarantee that $G(k,r)$ has no proper list coloring from $L$. This condition yields an upper bound on $r^*(k)$ on the order of $\sqrt{k \ln k}$. However, as explicitly noted in arXiv:2610.42094 following Corollary 1.4:
'Part (c) concerns only the lower bound produced by Theorem 1.3 ; it says nothing about the true choosability of $G(k,r)$ , which could be larger, nor about the true least $r$ for which $G(k,r)$ is uncolorable from its standard lists.'
The paper thus leaves the true value of $r^*(k)$ open. Whether $r^*(k) = \Theta(\sqrt{k \ln k})$, or whether uncolorability already sets in at some $r = o(\sqrt{k \ln k})$, is the natural question it raises; the paper gives no lower bound on $r^*(k)$.

Several baseline bounds and structural constraints on $G(k,r)$ and $r^*(k)$ were established prior to this work:

- The trivial upper bound: for any $k \ge 1$ and any $r \ge k$, the graph $G(k,r)$ has no proper list coloring from its standard lists, as formalized in `bipartite_subset_uncolorable_of_ge`. Indeed, because any two $k$-element subsets $S, T \subseteq [2k-1]$ satisfy $|S \cap T| \le k \le r$, every pair of vertices between $A$ and $B$ is connected by an edge. Thus $G(k,r)$ is a complete bipartite graph, which admits no proper standard list coloring, showing $r^*(k) \le k$.
- Threshold one colorability: for every $k \ge 2$, the graph $G(k,1)$ is colorable from its standard lists, as established in `bipartite_subset_colorable_at_one`. This yields the lower bound $r^*(k) \ge 2$ for all $k \ge 2$.
- Symmetry obstructions: at parameter $k = 6$ and threshold $r = 3$, it was shown in `op861_no_right_equivariant_k6_r3` that there do not exist two color selection functions on the $6$-subsets of $11$ cyclic colors that both choose available colors, differ on all pairs intersecting in at most $3$ elements, and satisfy cyclic equivariance on the second selector.

This post proves that $G(k, 2)$ is colorable from its standard lists for every $k \ge 5$ (`bipartite_subset_colorable_two_from_five`), so $r^*(k) \ge 3$ for all $k \ge 5$, one more than the threshold-one bound. The proof has two parts: a lifting lemma, valid for every threshold $r$, showing that a standard-list coloring of $G(k,r)$ yields one of $G(k+1,r)$ (so $r^*(k)$ never decreases as $k$ grows), and an explicit coloring of $G(5,2)$ described by one rule on $\mathbb{Z}_9$.
result:
The main theorem establishes that the bipartite subset graph with threshold $r = 2$ admits a proper list coloring from its standard lists for every integer $k \ge 5$.

Theorem 1 (`bipartite_subset_colorable_two_from_five`). For every integer $k \ge 5$, the bipartite subset graph $G(k, 2)$ is colorable from its standard list assignment:
$$\forall k \ge 5, \quad \text{bipartite\_subset\_standard\_list\_colorable } k\ 2.$$

Since the edge sets of $G(k,r)$ grow with $r$, a standard-list coloring of $G(k,2)$ is also one of $G(k,0)$ and $G(k,1)$, so Theorem 1 gives
$$r^*(k) \ge 3 \quad \text{for all } k \ge 5.$$

The two ingredients of the proof (Section 4) are of independent use. Lemma 2 holds for every threshold $r$: colorability of $G(k,r)$ from its standard lists implies that of $G(k+1,r)$, so for fixed $r$ the set of $k$ at which $G(k,r)$ is colorable is upward closed, and $r^*(k+1) \ge r^*(k)$. Lemma 1 is the base case $G(5,2)$. For comparison:

- In `bipartite_subset_colorable_at_one`, standard-list colorability was proved for threshold $r = 1$ for all $k \ge 2$, implying $r^*(k) \ge 2$ for all $k \ge 2$. Theorem 1 increases this lower bound to $r^*(k) \ge 3$ for all $k \ge 5$.
- In `bipartite_subset_uncolorable_of_ge`, it was shown that for any $k \ge 1$ and any $r \ge k$, the graph $G(k,r)$ is uncolorable from its standard lists, providing the general upper bound $r^*(k) \le k$.
- In `op861_no_right_equivariant_k6_r3`, it was proved that at $k = 6$ and $r = 3$, there are no two color selectors on the $6$-subsets of $11$ cyclic colors that both choose available colors, differ on every pair of subsets intersecting in at most $3$ elements, and have the second selector commute with every shift $z \mapsto z + d$ of $\mathbb{Z}_{11}$. This demonstrates that extending colorability results to threshold $r = 3$ requires techniques that break cyclic symmetry.
proof:
The theorem follows by induction on $k \ge 5$ from two lemmas: the base case $k = 5$ (Lemma 1) and the step from $k$ to $k+1$ at a fixed threshold (Lemma 2). In both it is convenient to restate colorability in terms of selectors: $G(k,r)$ is colorable from its standard lists if and only if there are maps $f, g$ from the $k$-subsets of a $(2k-1)$-element color set to colors with $f(S) \in S$, $g(T) \in T$, and $f(S) \ne g(T)$ whenever $|S \cap T| \le r$ (take $f = c$ on $A$ and $g = c$ on $B$). The selector form makes sense over any finite color set, and it is invariant under relabelling the colors by a bijection; Lean uses both facts.

Lemma 1 (`bipartite_subset_colorable_five_at_two`). $G(5,2)$ is colorable from its standard lists.

Proof. Identify the color set with $\mathbb{Z}_9$, and for $i \in \mathbb{Z}_9$ put
$$N(i) = \{i+2,\ i+3,\ i+4,\ i+5\},$$
a $4$-set not containing $i$. A finite check, done in Lean by `decide` over all $5$-subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_9$, shows that every $5$-set $S$ contains some $i$ with $|S \cap N(i)| \ge 3$. Let $p(S)$ be such an $i$, and use the same selector on both sides: $f = g = p$. Then $p(S) \in S$, so the lists are respected. Suppose $p(S) = p(T) = i$. The sets $S \cap N(i)$ and $T \cap N(i)$ are subsets of the $4$-set $N(i)$ of size at least $3$, so they share at least $3 + 3 - 4 = 2$ elements. These lie in $S \cap T$, and so does $i$, which is not in $N(i)$. Hence $|S \cap T| \ge 3$, and $a_S b_T$ is not an edge of $G(5,2)$. So equal colors never meet across an edge, and the coloring is proper. $\square$

Lemma 2 (`bipartite_subset_colorable_succ`). For all $k \ge 1$ and $r \ge 0$: if $G(k,r)$ is colorable from its standard lists, so is $G(k+1,r)$.

Proof. Let $f, g$ be selectors for $k$-subsets of a color set $P$ with $|P| = 2k-1$, and add two new colors $x_0, x_1$, so $|P \cup \{x_0, x_1\}| = 2k+1 = 2(k+1)-1$. For a $(k+1)$-subset $S$ of the new color set:

- if $S$ contains both $x_0$ and $x_1$, put $F(S) = x_0$ and $G(S) = x_1$;
- otherwise $S$ has at most one new color, hence at least $k$ old ones; choose a $k$-subset $U(S) \subseteq S \cap P$ and put $F(S) = f(U(S))$, $G(S) = g(U(S))$.

Both selectors pick from their own set. Let $|S \cap T| \le r$. If $S$ and $T$ both contain $x_0, x_1$, then $F(S) = x_0 \ne x_1 = G(T)$. If exactly one of them does, one color is new and the other old. If neither does, then $U(S) \cap U(T) \subseteq S \cap T$, so $|U(S) \cap U(T)| \le r$, and $F(S) = f(U(S)) \ne g(U(T)) = G(T)$. Relabelling the $2k+1$ colors as $\mathrm{Fin}(2(k+1)-1)$ gives a standard-list coloring of $G(k+1,r)$. $\square$

Proof of Theorem 1. Induction on $k \ge 5$: the base case is Lemma 1, and Lemma 2 with $r = 2$ (its hypothesis $1 \le k$ holds since $k \ge 5$) carries colorability from $k$ to $k+1$. $\square$
discussion:
The result `bipartite_subset_colorable_two_from_five` establishes that the bipartite subset graph $G(k, 2)$ is colorable from its standard lists for all $k \ge 5$, providing the uniform lower bound:
$$r^*(k) \ge 3 \quad \text{for all } k \ge 5.$$

While this strictly improves the previously known uniform lower bound $r^*(k) \ge 2$ (derived from `bipartite_subset_colorable_at_one` for $k \ge 2$), it leaves open the central asymptotic question formulated in arXiv:2610.42094. Theorem 1.3 of that paper proves that the condition $r^2 > 2(2k-1)\ln(2k-1)$ guarantees uncolorability from standard lists, showing that $r^*(k) = O(\sqrt{k \ln k})$. The paper notes that this bound says nothing about the true least $r$, which leaves open whether $r^*(k) = \Theta(\sqrt{k \ln k})$ or $r^*(k) = o(\sqrt{k \ln k})$ as $k \to \infty$.

A constant lower bound of $3$ does not distinguish between these asymptotic regimes. In particular, the current result does not determine whether $r^*(k)$ grows unboundedly with $k$ or remains bounded by an absolute constant. Determining whether $r^*(k) \to \infty$ as $k \to \infty$ is an essential step toward answering the question in arXiv:2610.42094.

The immediate next parameter value is $r = 3$. Determining whether $G(k, 3)$ admits a proper standard list coloring for large $k$—or even for specific values such as $k = 5$ or $k = 6$—remains open. However, the search for colorings at threshold $r = 3$ faces non-trivial symmetry obstructions. In `op861_no_right_equivariant_k6_r3`, it was shown that for $k = 6$ (where the ground set has $2k - 1 = 11$ colors), there are no two color selection functions on $\binom{\mathrm{Fin}(11)}{6}$ such that both choose available colors, differ whenever $|S \cap T| \le 3$, and satisfy cyclic equivariance on the second selector:
$$c_B(T + d) = c_B(T) + d \quad \text{for all } d \in \mathbb{Z}_{11}.$$
Since the problem is symmetric under exchanging $A$ and $B$, neither selector of a standard-list coloring of $G(6,3)$ (if one exists) can commute with all cyclic shifts. The rule of Lemma 1 is shift-invariant on $\mathbb{Z}_9$ (up to the choice among several admissible $i$), so a direct analogue of it at $k = 6$, $r = 3$ would have to break that symmetry.

Beyond $r = 3$, it remains an open challenge to establish non-trivial lower bounds on $r^*(k)$ that grow with $k$, and to narrow the gap between the constant lower bounds ($r^*(k) \ge 3$) and the upper bound from arXiv:2610.42094, the least integer $r$ with $r^2 > 2(2k-1)\ln(2k-1)$. By Lemma 2, a coloring of $G(k_0, r)$ for one $k_0$ settles every larger $k$ at that threshold, so a growing lower bound reduces to base cases $G(k_r, r)$ for a sequence of thresholds $r$; the rule of Lemma 1, a vertex choosing a color $i$ around which it is dense in a fixed window $N(i)$, is one candidate pattern for such base cases.
preliminaries:
We formalize the graphs, colorings, and parameters following the definitions used in the Lean formalization.

Throughout, for a positive integer $m$, we denote by $\mathrm{Fin}(m)$ the finite set $\{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$ of cardinality $m$. Subsets of size $k$ of $\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)$ are represented as elements of the subtype of subsets having cardinality $k$.

Definition 1 (Bipartite Subset Graph). For positive integers $k$ and non-negative integers $r$, the bipartite subset graph, denoted $G(k, r)$, is an undirected simple bipartite graph whose vertex set is partitioned into two disjoint sets:
$$V = A \sqcup B$$
where both $A$ and $B$ are copies of the family $\binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k}$ of all $k$-element subsets of $\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)$. In the Lean formalization, the vertex type is the sum type:
$$V = \left\{ S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}(2k-1) : |S| = k \right\} \oplus \left\{ T \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}(2k-1) : |T| = k \right\}$$
where vertices in $A$ are represented as terms of the left summand and vertices in $B$ are represented as terms of the right summand. The edge relation is defined so that no two vertices in $A$ are adjacent, no two vertices in $B$ are adjacent, and an edge connects $a_S \in A$ and $b_T \in B$ if and only if:
$$|S \cap T| \le r.$$

Remark 1. In Definition 1, the adjacency condition uses a weak inequality $|S \cap T| \le r$. For $r = 0$, an edge connects $a_S$ and $b_T$ if and only if $S$ and $T$ are disjoint. Because $S$ and $T$ are subsets of size $k$ in a ground set of size $2k-1$, the principle of inclusion-exclusion implies that:
$$|S \cap T| = |S| + |T| - |S \cup T| \ge 2k - (2k-1) = 1.$$
Therefore, for any two subsets $S, T \in \binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k}$, their intersection is never empty, so $|S \cap T| \ge 1$. Consequently, when $r = 0$, the edge set of $G(k, 0)$ is empty. When $r \ge k$, the inequality $|S \cap T| \le r$ holds for all $S$ and $T$ since $|S \cap T| \le |S| = k \le r$; hence $G(k, r)$ is the complete bipartite graph with parts of size $\binom{2k-1}{k}$.

Definition 2 (Standard List Assignment). For the bipartite subset graph $G(k, r)$, the standard list assignment $L$ assigns to each vertex its corresponding subset of colors:
$$L(a_S) = S, \quad L(b_T) = T.$$
In Lean, each subset $S$ is a term of a subtype representing a finset of colors in $\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)$ with cardinality $k$. The list assignment maps each vertex to its underlying subset of colors via the standard subtype projection on each summand.

Definition 3 (Standard List Colorability). The predicate `bipartite_subset_standard_list_colorable` $k$ $r$ asserts that there exists a proper graph coloring $c$ of $G(k, r)$ taking values in $\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)$ such that every vertex receives a color from its assigned list:
$$\text{bipartite\_subset\_standard\_list\_colorable } k\ r \iff \exists c : (G(k,r)).\text{Coloring}(\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)), \; \forall v \in V, \; c(v) \in L(v).$$
Unpacking the condition, this means there exist two selector functions:
$$c_A : \binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k} \to \mathrm{Fin}(2k-1) \quad \text{and} \quad c_B : \binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k} \to \mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)$$
satisfying:

1. List validity: $c_A(S) \in S$ for every $S \in \binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k}$, and $c_B(T) \in T$ for every $T \in \binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k}$;
2. Proper coloring: for all $S, T \in \binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k}$, if $|S \cap T| \le r$, then $c_A(S) \ne c_B(T)$.

Definition 4 (Least Uncolorable Threshold). The least uncolorable threshold parameter, denoted $r^*(k)$, is the minimal non-negative integer $r$ such that $G(k, r)$ is not colorable from its standard lists:
$$r^*(k) = \min \{ r \in \mathbb{N} : \neg \text{bipartite\_subset\_standard\_list\_colorable } k\ r \}.$$

Remark 2. The parameter $r^*(k)$ is well-defined for all $k \ge 1$ because, by `bipartite_subset_uncolorable_of_ge`, the graph is uncolorable whenever $r \ge k$, ensuring that the set $\{ r \in \mathbb{N} : \neg \text{bipartite\_subset\_standard\_list\_colorable } k\ r \}$ is non-empty and bounded above by $k$.

references.title: A Counterexample to the Alon-Krivelevich Conjecture and a New Lower Bound for Choosability of Bipartite Graphs

problem.title: Least intersection parameter for standard list uncolorability in bipartite subset graphs

research: Gives the uniform lower bound of three on the least uncolorable intersection threshold for every k at least five
tier_why: One threshold value: r = 2 for every k >= 5, from a finite base case k = 5 and a short lifting lemma (colorability passes from k to k+1); a constant lower bound that leaves the paper's asymptotic question open.

zh.title: 相交阈值为二的二部子集图对每一个不小于五的参数都是列表可染色的
zh.abstract: 对于整数 $k \ge 2$ 以及整数阈值 $r \ge 0$，二部子集图 $G(k,r)$ 具有顶点部类 $A$ 和 $B$，它们是 $\{1, \dots, 2k-1\}$ 的所有 $k$ 元子集族 $\binom{[2k-1]}{k}$ 的两个不相交副本，且在 $a_S \in A$ 与 $b_T \in B$ 之间存在一条边当且仅当 $|S \cap T| \le r$。为每个顶点分配其自身的子集作为其列表，并设 $r^*(k)$ 为使得这些标准列表不存在正常染色的最小 $r$。arXiv:2610.42094 表明 $r^2 > 2(2k-1)\ln(2k-1)$ 会导致不可染色性，从而 $r^*(k) = O(\sqrt{k \ln k})$，并指出其方法对于真正的最小 $r$ 未给出任何信息。我们在另一方面证明了两个事实。第一，在固定阈值 $r$ 下的标准列表可染色性可由 $k$ 传递至 $k+1$，因此 $r^*(k)$ 关于 $k$ 是非递减的。第二，通过在两侧使用 $\mathbb{Z}_9$ 上的单一规则，$G(5,2)$ 从其标准列表中是可染色的。两者结合可得，对于每一个 $k \ge 5$，$G(k,2)$ 从其标准列表中都是可染色的，即对所有 $k \ge 5$ 均有 $r^*(k) \ge 3$。所有命题均已在 Lean 4 中得到验证。
zh.introduction:
图的列表色数或选择数是图论中的一个核心参数。在 arXiv:2610.42094 中，一项关于二部图列表可染色性的研究引入了一族二部子集图，它们在标准列表分配下的列表可染色性性质提供了二部图选择数的下界。

对于整数 $k \ge 2$ 和整数 $r \ge 0$，二部子集图 $G(k,r)$ 定义为具有两个顶点部类 $A$ 与 $B$，二者均同构于具有 $2k-1$ 个元素的基础集（记为 $[2k-1] = \{1, \dots, 2k-1\}$）的所有 $k$ 元子集族 $\binom{[2k-1]}{k}$。两个顶点 $a_S \in A$ 与 $b_T \in B$ 之间有边相连当且仅当其定义子集满足相交条件 $|S \cap T| \le r$。在 $A$ 内部或 $B$ 内部不存在边，这使得 $G(k,r)$ 成为一个二部图。每个顶点都被分配其下标子集作为其可用颜色列表：对所有 $a_S \in A$ 有 $L(a_S) = S$，对所有 $b_T \in B$ 有 $L(b_T) = T$。来自这些标准列表的正常列表染色是指为每个 $a_S \in A$ 选择一种颜色 $c(a_S) \in S$，并为每个 $b_T \in B$ 选择一种颜色 $c(b_T) \in T$，使得只要 $|S \cap T| \le r$，所选的颜色就不同：$c(a_S) \ne c(b_T)$。

最小不可染色相交参数 $r^*(k)$ 定义为使得 $G(k,r)$ 从其标准列表分配 $L$ 不存在正常列表染色的最小整数 $r \ge 0$。在 arXiv:2610.42094 中，定理 1.3 确立了条件 $r^2 > 2(2k-1)\ln(2k-1)$ 足以保证 $G(k,r)$ 从 $L$ 不存在正常列表染色。该条件给出了 $r^*(k)$ 的一个量级为 $\sqrt{k \ln k}$ 的上界。然而，正如 arXiv:2610.42094 在推论 1.4 之后明确指出的：
'Part (c) concerns only the lower bound produced by Theorem 1.3 ; it says nothing about the true choosability of $G(k,r)$ , which could be larger, nor about the true least $r$ for which $G(k,r)$ is uncolorable from its standard lists.'
该论文因此将 $r^*(k)$ 的真实值留作公开问题。$r^*(k) = \Theta(\sqrt{k \ln k})$ 还是在某个 $r = o(\sqrt{k \ln k})$ 处就已经开始出现不可染色性，是它所提出的自然问题；该论文未给出 $r^*(k)$ 的任何下界。

在这项工作之前，已经确立了关于 $G(k,r)$ 和 $r^*(k)$ 的若干基准界和结构限制：

- 平凡上界：对于任意 $k \ge 1$ 以及任意 $r \ge k$，图 $G(k,r)$ 从其标准列表中不存在正常列表染色，这已在 `bipartite_subset_uncolorable_of_ge` 中形式化。事实上，因为任意两个 $k$ 元子集 $S, T \subseteq [2k-1]$ 都满足 $|S \cap T| \le k \le r$，所以 $A$ 与 $B$ 之间的每一对顶点都由一条边相连。因此 $G(k,r)$ 是一个完全二部图，它不容许任何正常的标准列表染色，从而表明 $r^*(k) \le k$。
- 阈值一的可染色性：对于每一个 $k \ge 2$，图 $G(k,1)$ 从其标准列表中是可染色的，这已在 `bipartite_subset_colorable_at_one` 中确立。这给出了对所有 $k \ge 2$ 均成立的下界 $r^*(k) \ge 2$。
- 对称性阻碍：在参数 $k = 6$ 和阈值 $r = 3$ 处，`op861_no_right_equivariant_k6_r3` 中证明了，在 $11$ 种循环颜色的 $6$ 元子集上不存在两个颜色选择函数，使得它们都选择可用颜色、在相交至多 $3$ 个元素的所有子集对上均取不同值，并且第二个选择器满足循环等变性。

本博文证明对于每个 $k \ge 5$，$G(k, 2)$ 从其标准列表中都是可染色的（`bipartite_subset_colorable_two_from_five`），因此对所有 $k \ge 5$ 均有 $r^*(k) \ge 3$，这比阈值一的界大了一。该证明包含两个部分：一个对每个阈值 $r$ 均成立的提升引理，表明 $G(k,r)$ 的标准列表染色可诱导出 $G(k+1,r)$ 的标准列表染色（因此 $r^*(k)$ 随着 $k$ 的增长绝不减少）；以及一个通过 $\mathbb{Z}_9$ 上的单一规则给出的 $G(5,2)$ 的显式染色。
zh.preliminaries:
我们遵循 Lean 形式化中使用的定义来形式化图、染色和参数。

在全文中，对于正整数 $m$，我们用 $\mathrm{Fin}(m)$ 表示基数为 $m$ 的有限集 $\{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$。$\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)$ 的大小为 $k$ 的子集表示为基数为 $k$ 的子集构成的子类型（subtype）的元素。

定义 1（二部子集图）. 对于正整数 $k$ 和非负整数 $r$，二部子集图（记为 $G(k, r)$）是一个无向简单二部图，其顶点集划分为两个不相交的集合：
$$V = A \sqcup B$$
其中 $A$ 与 $B$ 都是 $\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)$ 的所有 $k$ 元子集族 $\binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k}$ 的副本。在 Lean 形式化中，顶点类型为和类型（sum type）：
$$V = \left\{ S \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}(2k-1) : |S| = k \right\} \oplus \left\{ T \subseteq \mathrm{Fin}(2k-1) : |T| = k \right\}$$
其中 $A$ 中的顶点表示为左直和项的项，$B$ 中的顶点表示为右直和项的项。边关系的定义使得 $A$ 中的任意两个顶点均不相邻，$B$ 中的任意两个顶点均不相邻，并且一条边连接 $a_S \in A$ 与 $b_T \in B$ 当且仅当：
$$|S \cap T| \le r.$$

注 1. 在定义 1 中，邻接条件使用的是弱不等式 $|S \cap T| \le r$。对于 $r = 0$，一条边连接 $a_S$ 与 $b_T$ 当且仅当 $S$ 与 $T$ 不相交。因为 $S$ 与 $T$ 是大小为 $2k-1$ 的基础集中的大小为 $k$ 的子集，容斥原理表明：
$$|S \cap T| = |S| + |T| - |S \cup T| \ge 2k - (2k-1) = 1.$$
因此，对于任意两个子集 $S, T \in \binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k}$，它们的交集永不为空，所以 $|S \cap T| \ge 1$。从而，当 $r = 0$ 时，$G(k, 0)$ 的边集为空。当 $r \ge k$ 时，由于 $|S \cap T| \le |S| = k \le r$，不等式 $|S \cap T| \le r$ 对所有 $S$ 和 $T$ 均成立；因此 $G(k, r)$ 是两个部的顶点数均为 $\binom{2k-1}{k}$ 的完全二部图。

定义 2（标准列表分配）. 对于二部子集图 $G(k, r)$，标准列表分配 $L$ 为每个顶点分配其对应的颜色子集：
$$L(a_S) = S, \quad L(b_T) = T.$$
在 Lean 中，每个子集 $S$ 都是一个子类型的项，该子类型表示 $\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)$ 中基数为 $k$ 的有限颜色集合（finset）。列表分配通过在每个直和项上的标准子类型投影，将每个顶点映射到其底层的颜色子集。

定义 3（标准列表可染色性）. 谓词 `bipartite_subset_standard_list_colorable` $k$ $r$ 断言存在一个取值于 $\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)$ 的 $G(k, r)$ 的正常图染色 $c$，使得每个顶点都从其所分配的列表中获得一种颜色：
$$\text{bipartite\_subset\_standard\_list\_colorable } k\ r \iff \exists c : (G(k,r)).\text{Coloring}(\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)), \; \forall v \in V, \; c(v) \in L(v).$$
展开该条件，这意味着存在两个选择器函数：
$$c_A : \binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k} \to \mathrm{Fin}(2k-1) \quad \text{and} \quad c_B : \binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k} \to \mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)$$
满足：

1. 列表有效性：对每个 $S \in \binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k}$ 有 $c_A(S) \in S$，且对每个 $T \in \binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k}$ 有 $c_B(T) \in T$；
2. 正常染色：对所有 $S, T \in \binom{\mathrm{Fin}(2k-1)}{k}$，若 $|S \cap T| \le r$，则 $c_A(S) \ne c_B(T)$。

定义 4（最小不可染阈值）. 最小不可染阈值参数（记为 $r^*(k)$）是使得 $G(k, r)$ 从其标准列表中不可染色的最小非负整数 $r$：
$$r^*(k) = \min \{ r \in \mathbb{N} : \neg \text{bipartite\_subset\_standard\_list\_colorable } k\ r \}.$$

注 2. 参数 $r^*(k)$ 对所有 $k \ge 1$ 都是良定义的，因为根据 `bipartite_subset_uncolorable_of_ge`，只要 $r \ge k$ 图就是不可染色的，这保证了集合 $\{ r \in \mathbb{N} : \neg \text{bipartite\_subset\_standard\_list\_colorable } k\ r \}$ 非空且以 $k$ 为上界。
zh.result:
主定理确立了对于每个整数 $k \ge 5$，阈值 $r = 2$ 的二部子集图容许来自其标准列表的正常列表染色。

定理 1 (`bipartite_subset_colorable_two_from_five`). 对于每个整数 $k \ge 5$，二部子集图 $G(k, 2)$ 从其标准列表分配中是可染色的：
$$\forall k \ge 5, \quad \text{bipartite\_subset\_standard\_list\_colorable } k\ 2.$$

由于 $G(k,r)$ 的边集随 $r$ 的增大而增大，因此 $G(k,2)$ 的标准列表染色也是 $G(k,0)$ 和 $G(k,1)$ 的标准列表染色，故定理 1 给出
$$r^*(k) \ge 3 \quad \text{for all } k \ge 5.$$

该证明的两个组成部分（第 4 节）具有独立的用途。引理 2 对每一个阈值 $r$ 都成立：$G(k,r)$ 从其标准列表中的可染色性蕴涵 $G(k+1,r)$ 的可染色性，因此对于固定的 $r$，使得 $G(k,r)$ 可染色的 $k$ 的集合是向上封闭的，且 $r^*(k+1) \ge r^*(k)$。引理 1 是基础情形 $G(5,2)$。作为对比：

- 在 `bipartite_subset_colorable_at_one` 中，对所有 $k \ge 2$ 证明了阈值 $r = 1$ 处的标准列表可染色性，这蕴涵了对所有 $k \ge 2$ 均有 $r^*(k) \ge 2$。定理 1 将该下界提高至对所有 $k \ge 5$ 均有 $r^*(k) \ge 3$。
- 在 `bipartite_subset_uncolorable_of_ge` 中表明，对于任意 $k \ge 1$ 以及任意 $r \ge k$，图 $G(k,r)$ 从其标准列表中都是不可染色的，从而给出了通用的上界 $r^*(k) \le k$。
- 在 `op861_no_right_equivariant_k6_r3` 中证明了，在 $k = 6$ 且 $r = 3$ 处，在 $11$ 种循环颜色的 $6$ 元子集上不存在两个颜色选择器，使得它们既选择可用颜色，又在相交至多 $3$ 个元素的所有子集对上均取不同值，并且使得第二个选择器与 $\mathbb{Z}_{11}$ 的每个平移变换 $z \mapsto z + d$ 都可交换。这表明将可染色性结果推广至阈值 $r = 3$ 需要打破循环对称性的技术。
zh.proof:
该定理通过对 $k \ge 5$ 进行归纳，由两个引理得出：基础情形 $k = 5$（引理 1）以及在固定阈值下从 $k$ 到 $k+1$ 的递推步（引理 2）。在这两处，用选择器来重新表述可染色性都很方便：$G(k,r)$ 从其标准列表中可染色当且仅当存在从一个 $(2k-1)$ 元颜色集的 $k$ 元子集映至颜色的映射 $f, g$，满足 $f(S) \in S$、$g(T) \in T$，且只要 $|S \cap T| \le r$ 就有 $f(S) \ne g(T)$（在 $A$ 上取 $f = c$，在 $B$ 上取 $g = c$）。选择器形式在任意有限颜色集上都是有意义的，并且在通过双射重新标记颜色下是不变量；Lean 同时利用了这两个事实。

引理 1 (`bipartite_subset_colorable_five_at_two`). $G(5,2)$ 从其标准列表中是可染色的。

证明. 将颜色集等同于 $\mathbb{Z}_9$，对于 $i \in \mathbb{Z}_9$，令
$$N(i) = \{i+2,\ i+3,\ i+4,\ i+5\},$$
这是一个不包含 $i$ 的 $4$ 元集。在 Lean 中通过对 $\mathbb{Z}_9$ 的所有 $5$ 元子集调用 `decide` 进行有限验证表明，每个 $5$ 元集 $S$ 都包含某个满足 $|S \cap N(i)| \ge 3$ 的 $i$。设 $p(S)$ 为这样的一个 $i$，并在两侧使用相同的选择器：$f = g = p$。由于 $p(S) \in S$，因而遵循了列表要求。假设 $p(S) = p(T) = i$。集合 $S \cap N(i)$ 与 $T \cap N(i)$ 是 $4$ 元集 $N(i)$ 的大小至少为 $3$ 的子集，因此它们至少共享 $3 + 3 - 4 = 2$ 个元素。这些元素位于 $S \cap T$ 中，而不在 $N(i)$ 中的 $i$ 也位于 $S \cap T$ 中。因此 $|S \cap T| \ge 3$，$a_S b_T$ 不是 $G(5,2)$ 的边。因此相同的颜色绝不会在一条边两端相遇，该染色是正常的。$\square$

引理 2 (`bipartite_subset_colorable_succ`). 对所有 $k \ge 1$ 以及 $r \ge 0$：若 $G(k,r)$ 从其标准列表中是可染色的，则 $G(k+1,r)$ 亦然。

证明. 设 $f, g$ 为具有 $|P| = 2k-1$ 的颜色集 $P$ 的 $k$ 元子集选择器，添加两种新颜色 $x_0, x_1$，从而 $|P \cup \{x_0, x_1\}| = 2k+1 = 2(k+1)-1$。对于新颜色集的一个 $(k+1)$ 元子集 $S$：

- 若 $S$ 同时包含 $x_0$ 和 $x_1$，令 $F(S) = x_0$ 以及 $G(S) = x_1$；
- 否则 $S$ 至多包含一种新颜色，从而至少包含 $k$ 种旧颜色；选取一个 $k$ 元子集 $U(S) \subseteq S \cap P$ 并令 $F(S) = f(U(S))$，$G(S) = g(U(S))$。

两个选择器均从各自的集合中选取颜色。设 $|S \cap T| \le r$。若 $S$ 和 $T$ 均包含 $x_0, x_1$，则 $F(S) = x_0 \ne x_1 = G(T)$。若它们之中恰有一个包含，则一种颜色是新的而另一种是旧的。若两者均不包含，则 $U(S) \cap U(T) \subseteq S \cap T$，因此 $|U(S) \cap U(T)| \le r$，且 $F(S) = f(U(S)) \ne g(U(T)) = G(T)$。将这 $2k+1$ 种颜色重新标记为 $\mathrm{Fin}(2(k+1)-1)$ 即可给出 $G(k+1,r)$ 的标准列表染色。$\square$

定理 1 的证明. 对 $k \ge 5$ 进行归纳：基础情形是引理 1，而取 $r = 2$ 的引理 2（其假设 $1 \le k$ 由于 $k \ge 5$ 而成立）将可染色性从 $k$ 传递至 $k+1$。$\square$
zh.discussion:
结果 `bipartite_subset_colorable_two_from_five` 确立了对所有 $k \ge 5$，二部子集图 $G(k, 2)$ 从其标准列表中都是可染色的，从而给出了一致下界：
$$r^*(k) \ge 3 \quad \text{for all } k \ge 5.$$

虽然这严格改进了先前已知的一致下界 $r^*(k) \ge 2$（由 $k \ge 2$ 时的 `bipartite_subset_colorable_at_one` 导出），但它仍未解决 arXiv:2610.42094 中提出的核心渐近问题。该论文的定理 1.3 证明了条件 $r^2 > 2(2k-1)\ln(2k-1)$ 保证了从标准列表中不可染色，表明 $r^*(k) = O(\sqrt{k \ln k})$。该论文指出，该界对于真正的最小 $r$ 未给出任何信息，这使得当 $k \to \infty$ 时是 $r^*(k) = \Theta(\sqrt{k \ln k})$ 还是 $r^*(k) = o(\sqrt{k \ln k})$ 仍为一个未决问题。

常数下界 $3$ 无法区分这些渐近态势。特别是，当前结果并没有确定 $r^*(k)$ 是随 $k$ 无界增长，还是被某个绝对常数所界定。确定当 $k \to \infty$ 时是否有 $r^*(k) \to \infty$，是回答 arXiv:2610.42094 中问题的关键一步。

紧接着的下一个参数值是 $r = 3$。确定对于较大的 $k$——乃至对于诸如 $k = 5$ 或 $k = 6$ 的特定值——$G(k, 3)$ 是否容许正常的标准列表染色，仍然是未决的。然而，在阈值 $r = 3$ 处寻找染色面临着非平凡的对称性阻碍。在 `op861_no_right_equivariant_k6_r3` 中证明了，对于 $k = 6$（此时基础集有 $2k - 1 = 11$ 种颜色），在 $\binom{\mathrm{Fin}(11)}{6}$ 上不存在两个颜色选择函数，使得二者均选择可用颜色、只要 $|S \cap T| \le 3$ 就取不同值，并且第二个选择器满足循环等变性：
$$c_B(T + d) = c_B(T) + d \quad \text{for all } d \in \mathbb{Z}_{11}.$$
由于该问题在交换 $A$ 和 $B$ 下是对称的，因此 $G(6,3)$ 的标准列表染色（如果存在的话）的两个选择器都无法与所有循环平移对易。引理 1 的规则在 $\mathbb{Z}_9$ 上是平移不变的（在若干个容许的 $i$ 之间的选择除外），因此它在 $k = 6$，$r = 3$ 处的直接类似物必须打破这种对称性。

在 $r = 3$ 之外，建立随 $k$ 增长的 $r^*(k)$ 的非平凡下界，以及缩小常数下界（$r^*(k) \ge 3$）与来自 arXiv:2610.42094 的上界（即满足 $r^2 > 2(2k-1)\ln(2k-1)$ 的最小整数 $r$）之间的差距，仍然是一个悬而未决的挑战。根据引理 2，对于某个 $k_0$ 的 $G(k_0, r)$ 的染色可以解决该阈值下所有更大的 $k$，因此增长的下界归结为一系列阈值 $r$ 的基础情形 $G(k_r, r)$；引理 1 的规则——顶点选择一种颜色 $i$，使其在固定窗口 $N(i)$ 内围绕 $i$ 是稠密的——正是此类基础情形的一个候选模式。
